GPTQ uses an approximate second-order reconstruction objective to quantize weights sequentially and compensate remaining weights for quantization error. AWQ identifies activation-sensitive channels and rescales them to preserve important weights. SmoothQuant applies an equivalent channel scaling that shifts difficult activation magnitudes into weights, enabling lower-precision activation computation. [1](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.17323) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.00978) [3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.10438)

$$XW=(XD^{-1})(DW).$$

Activation outliers can vary across inputs and channels, so one shared scale wastes most quantization bins on extremes. Weights are fixed and easier to inspect/calibrate once. Per-channel or block scales help but add metadata and kernel complexity. Evaluate representative calibration data, out-of-domain inputs, long sequences, and end-to-end kernel support: a numerically valid compressed model is not automatically faster on a given GPU.
